conceptual assets.information: The result word is the rs1_i value when the recognized conditional operation passes, and zero otherwise; the coprocessor's use depends on returning this word to the CPU.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because res_o exposes the rs1-derived value at line 54. Integrity is at risk because lines 53-56 allow the condition and valid-command decode to replace the result with zero. Availability is at risk because the same gating can withhold the rs1-derived result by selecting zero at lines 53-56.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter the command or condition path to force zero instead of the intended result, or observe res_o to obtain a secret operand value.

conceptual assets.information: The rs2_i word supplies the operand whose zero or nonzero property determines the conditional operation; the operation depends on this input even though the word itself is not returned.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because the zero-versus-rs1 behavior of res_o at lines 53-56 can disclose the operand's zero or nonzero property. Integrity is at risk because changing rs2_i changes rs2_zero at line 62 and can change the returned result. Availability is at risk because that changed predicate can prevent the intended rs1_i value from passing to res_o at lines 53-56.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could modify rs2_i or observe the conditional result to alter or infer the comparison operand's predicate.

conceptual assets.information: This decision represents whether the instruction's zero or nonzero predicate is satisfied and selects whether rs1_i or zero is written to res_o; it is computed internally and has no standalone boundary exit because it only controls the result.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because the selected value at res_o can reveal the decision at lines 53-56. Integrity is at risk because condition directly decides the result assignment at line 53. Availability is at risk because condition can block the intended result value and select zero at lines 53-56.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could tamper with the condition computation at line 63 to force or suppress the conditional result and infer the predicate from res_o.

conceptual assets.information: This indication reports whether ctrl_i encodes the supported conditional coprocessor operation; downstream logic depends on valid_o to recognize and use the operation result.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because the decode at lines 41-43 drives valid_o at line 66, so tampering can falsely accept an unsupported command or reject a supported one. Availability is at risk because deasserting valid_o at line 66 can prevent downstream logic from accepting the operation.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could tamper with the command-valid decode so that valid_o rejects the operation or falsely validates an unsupported command.

considered, not kept.reason: The opcode and function fields that only select or name the coprocessor operation are barred as separate pieces by the Operation selectors rule.
clk_i and rstn_i are excluded as conceptual assets by the clocks-and-resets rule because they only time or reset res_o.
